title: Architecture model
description: Architecture as code, independent of notation. The model carries TOPOLOGICAL and ORDINAL facts only, never metric ones: anything with a unit -- pixels, points, millimetres, a colour, a font -- describes how one particular tool paints the model, not the architecture. The test for any future field: apply a monotone transformation to it (double it, add one to every value); if the diagram still says the same thing it is ordinal and may enter, and if the meaning changes it is metric and belongs in a render profile. Shape, colour and drawn size therefore live in a separate render profile (examples/c4.render.json), chosen by whoever invokes the exporter and never referenced from the model.

scope.description: What this model covers. Structurizr calls it scope and demands it: without it, a reader cannot tell a landscape from a single system.

spec.description: The types this model uses. This is where C4, UML or any other notation stops being hardwired and becomes a declaration.

extends.description: URL of another spec this one refines. Lets us publish 'c4.json' or 'uml.json' and start from there.

nodes.description: Everything is a node: a system, a UML class, a decision or a document. What tells them apart is their type, not their position in a class hierarchy.

views.description: A view states WHAT to include, it does not enumerate elements: it stays correct as the model grows.

contains.description: Which types it admits inside. Absent = any, which is how free nesting is achieved. Empty list = it is a leaf.

requires.description: Fields a node of this type must carry. This is what makes the model checkable.

from.description: Node types admitted as source. Absent = any.

origin.description: Where this fact came from. A model extracted from a machine can state what produced it and when, to tell what was measured from what was assumed.

include.description: A query, not a list. '*' is everything; also by type, by tag, or the neighbors of a node.

placement.description: Where a node sits, as a CELL and not as pixels. rank is the reading depth (row in a top-down view) and order the position within that rank; both are relative to the parent, so nesting composes and inserting a node shifts a column instead of breaking every coordinate. Measured reason for choosing cells: across dagre, elk and dot the vertical ORDER survives (0-1.1% of pairs invert) while the coordinates do not (only 22-69% of nodes keep their nearest neighbour). This normalises the part that is already reproducible and leaves the pixels to the exporter.

span.description: How many cells wide it is; for a node that groups others.

layout.description: Optional and PARTIAL overlay on top of the view. It does not change membership: the query still decides who appears. A node the query returns and this layout does not mention is valid -- the exporter places it and marks it derived. Without that rule two correct implementations would disagree, the same defect already fixed in the doc/date ambiguity.

direction.description: Reading direction. Fixes what rank means.

origin.description: Where this geometry comes from, mirroring the model's own origin field: stated by a person, or produced by a tool. There is no 'solver' value -- a layout that came out of dagre is imported, and tool says which one.

tool.description: Which tool produced it, with its version: 'dagre@11.4.1'.

modelDigest.description: Digest of the element set the query returned when this layout was written, and of NOTHING else. Lets a reader detect a stale layout. Reproducing a drawing takes three digests -- model, layout and render profile -- and keeping them apart is what stops the render profile from silently becoming part of the model.
